definitions.full: H400. okel אֹ֫כֶל 40 noun masculine Gen 41:36 food (Arabic , Aramaic אוּכְלָא , , Assyrian akalu Dl W , Ethiopic ) — ׳א absolute 41:35 +; construct 41:35 , 48 ; suffix אָכְלֶ֑ךָ Lev 25:37 ; אָכְלו Mal 1:12 , etc.; — Hexateuch mostly J E D, not Ezekiel — food, food-supply , especially cereals of store in Egypt Gen 41:35 (twice in verse) + 12 t. Genesis 41-44; 47:24 ; compare 14:11 (JE); also Lev 11:34 ; 25:37 (P) Deut 2:6 , 28 (D); א ׳נֶשֶׁךְ usury of food 23:20 (D) (|| ׳נ כֶּסֶף , etc.); הָאֹבֶל לְעֵת at meal-time Ruth 2:14 ; in poetry 17 t.; — food Psa 107:18 ; of offerings Mal 1:12 ; particular food Job 12:11 (as tasted); 36:31 (as given by God) so Psa 145:15 ; ׳א נָפֶ֑שׁ לְהָשִׁיב Lam 1:11 compare 1:19 ; especially cereals Prov 13:23 ; Joel 1:16 ; Hab 3:17 ; but also flesh Psa 78:18 ; 78:30 ; of food (prey) of wild animals 104:21 (|| טרף ):27; of prey of eagles Job 9:26 ; 39:29 ; ravens 38:41 .

Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?”
They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”
If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food;
and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.
We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”
He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
Our father said, ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’

It will happen at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts will be your own, for seed of the field, for your food, for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.”

and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls. You shall make your count for the lamb according to what everyone can eat.

“This is the thing which Yahweh has commanded: ‘Gather of it everyone according to his eating; an omer* An omer is about 2.2 liters or about 2.3 quarts a head, according to the number of your persons, you shall take it, every man for those who are in his tent.’ ”
When they measured it with an omer, he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack. They each gathered according to his eating.
They gathered it morning by morning, everyone according to his eating. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
All food which may be eaten which is soaked in water shall be unclean. All drink that may be drunk in every such vessel shall be unclean.
You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit.
You shall purchase food from them for money, that you may eat. You shall also buy water from them for money, that you may drink.’ ”
You shall sell me food for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink. Just let me pass through on my feet,
You may charge a foreigner interest; but you shall not your brother interest, that Yahweh your God may bless you in all that you put your hand to, in the land where you go in to possess it.
At meal time Boaz said to her, “Come here, and eat some bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar.”
They have passed away as the swift ships,
Doesn’t the ear try words,
There was nothing left that he didn’t devour,
For by these he judges the people.
Who provides for the raven his prey,
From there he spies out the prey.
They tempted God in their heart
They didn’t turn from their cravings.
The young lions roar after their prey,
These all wait for you,
Their soul abhors all kinds of food.
The eyes of all wait for you.
